title: Reckoning the Allowance Taken Back From a Healthy Options Card at a Period End
content:
This is the reconciliation basis on which the allowance taken back from a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card at the close of a benefit period is reckoned.

**1. The amount.** The amount taken back is what is unspent from that period's allowance less what may carry forward, never less than nothing, rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier step.

**2. What is unspent.** What is unspent from that period's allowance is the allowance loaded for the period, together with the money put back into it, less what was spent from the card in it and less anything already taken back from it, never less than nothing. What has already been taken back from it is the total of the allowance already taken back for that same period on the card's own record.

**3. Counting the benefit periods.** The benefit periods that have passed are counted as the whole quarters of the benefit year gone by where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters, and as the whole months gone by where it is loaded on calendar months. For this counting a benefit period runs 3 months where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year, 12 months where it is made available once a year, and 1 month in every other case; the months are taken from the first day of the benefit year to the day the reckoning is made.

**4. Which period is being closed.** The period whose allowance is being taken back is the period that ended one whole period before the current one, counting back from the periods that have passed and from how long an allowance stands. The period is named by the quarter of the benefit year it falls in.

**5. What may carry forward.** What may carry forward is the share the card allows of the base it is measured on, and never more than what is unspent; the rest is taken back.

**6. The standing values.** An allowance stands only to the last day of the benefit period it was loaded for. The allowance loaded for that period is taken as the quarterly allowance the card's tier carries. What was spent from the card in that period is taken as the total of every transaction posted in it. No money put back is counted into that period. Nothing carries forward, so the whole of what is unspent is taken back.

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** Take a card whose tier carries a quarterly allowance of 135.00 USD, on which the period being closed shows transactions posted of 88.20 USD and no allowance already taken back for it. What is unspent is 135.00 USD less 88.20 USD, that is 46.80 USD. Nothing carries forward, so the amount taken back is 46.80 USD, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end. Had the transactions posted come to 150.00 USD, the subtraction would fall below nothing and what is unspent is held at nothing, so nothing is taken back.
